Name: Varicose Veins Treatment in Ahmedabad
Department Details:
Varicose Veins & Causes

Varicose veins are twisted, swollen veins. Varicose veins can occur anywhere in the body, but they are most frequent in the legs. Varicose veins are not a life-threatening medical problem. They can, however, be uncomfortable and lead to more significant issues. Increased blood pressure in the veins causes varicose veins. Varicose veins develop in the veins near the skin’s surface (superficial).

People looking for varicose veins evaluation in Ahmedabad can consult the vascular care team at Bankers Vascular Centre. Assessment may include clinical examination and vascular ultrasound when appropriate to understand the affected veins and help determine suitable treatment options.

Learn more about Dr. Mohal Banker, Interventional Radiologist and Director at Bankers Vascular Centre.

Causes :

  • Weak or damaged vein walls and valves
  • Increased blood pressure in the veins
  • Pregnancy
  • Being overweight or obese
  • Sitting or standing for long periods
  • An inactive lifestyle
  • Family history of varicose vein

Symptoms

  • Itching, color changes, or dry, scaly skin
  • Swollen ankles or legs
  • Pain, aching, or a feeling of heaviness
  • Leg fatigue
  • Exercise intolerance

‍

Home treatments

  • Wearing compression stockings
  • Elevating your legs
  • Exercising regularly, especially walking
  • Managing weight
  • Avoiding salt
  • Wearing low-heeled shoes
  • Avoiding tight clothing

‍

Non-Surgical Solutions for Varicose Veins

Endovenous Laser Treatment (EVLT) is a minimally invasive treatment used to close affected superficial veins. Suitability and expected outcomes depend on clinical evaluation and the pattern of venous disease.

EVLT uses laser energy through a catheter to close an affected vein. It may be considered for suitable patients after clinical evaluation; recovery and aftercare vary by procedure and patient.

‍

2] VenaSeal is a minimally invasive procedure in which medical adhesive may be used to close an affected vein. Suitability depends on symptoms, ultrasound findings and clinical evaluation.

How it works

  1. A doctor uses ultrasound to locate the affected veins
  2. A catheter is inserted into the vein
  3. A small amount of medical glue is injected into the vein
  4. The vein walls are pressed together to help the glue set
  5. The process is repeated down the length of the vein


Benefits

  • Minimally invasive treatment approaches may use small access points or catheter-based techniques
  • Conventional open surgery may be avoided in appropriately selected cases
  • Treatment may be directed at affected veins
  • Some procedures may be performed as outpatient or day-care treatment, depending on the procedure and patient
  • Recovery requirements vary by procedure and individual clinical circumstances

The expected benefits, limitations and risks should be discussed during medical evaluation.

What happens after treatment

After treatment, care and follow-up depend on the procedure and individual clinical circumstances. Patients should follow instructions from their treating healthcare team, including activity, compression or follow-up guidance where recommended.
